ai-hpc.h3: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face in $12.9 billion open source deal
ai-hpc.summary: Nvidia has reportedly agreed to acquire the open model repository Hugging Face for about $12.9 billion, which would be its largest acquisition ever.
body: The Information reported that Nvidia agreed to buy Hugging Face, the GitHub-style hub where developers publish and download open weight models and datasets, for roughly $12.9 billion. Multiple outlets stress the deal is not yet signed and announced, so the terms could still move.

If it closes it would dwarf the $6.9 billion Nvidia paid for Mellanox in 2020. Nvidia already invested in Hugging Face in 2023 and, according to the Financial Times, offered a further $500 million at the end of 2025 at a $7 billion valuation. Hugging Face turned that round down because it did not want one dominant shareholder steering its decisions.

ai-hpc.h3: Nvidia pauses AI cloud revenue sharing plan over antitrust worries
ai-hpc.summary: Nvidia has stepped back from a financing scheme that gave credit support to smaller AI cloud firms in return for a cut of their rental revenue.
body: Less than two months after unveiling the AI Compute Partnership in July, Nvidia paused parts of the programme, the Wall Street Journal reported. The structure gave the chipmaker two bites of the same workload, first from selling accelerators and then from taking half of any rental income above an agreed base threshold.

Internal pushback drove the retreat. Some Nvidia staff warned current and prospective customers that the arrangement could attract antitrust scrutiny given how much of the compute market already runs through the company.

ai-hpc.h3: a16z raises $1.1 billion Machine Age fund for AI hardware
ai-hpc.summary: Andreessen Horowitz has closed its first fund dedicated to the physical layer of AI, covering chips, memory, interconnect, power and robotics.
body: The firm most associated with the phrase software is eating the world raised $1.1 billion for a hardware vehicle it calls the Machine Age Fund. Partners said the money will go into processors, memory, networking, storage, cooling, power delivery and robotics rather than applications.

Ben Horowitz framed AI alongside the microprocessor, the steam engine and electricity, arguing each needed an entirely new physical world built around it. Raghu Raghuram called AI infrastructure the largest infrastructure opportunity in the history of computing.

ai-hpc.h3: SK Hynix breaks ground on $4 billion Indiana HBM packaging plant
ai-hpc.summary: The memory maker started construction of its first US advanced packaging site, with mass production of next generation HBM due in the second half of 2029.
body: SK Hynix held a groundbreaking ceremony in Purdue Research Park for a $4 billion advanced memory packaging facility. The plant will package high bandwidth memory rather than fabricate the underlying wafers, which remain a Korean operation.

Company executives said Indiana will become a key memory production base by 2030, with HBM4E output targeted for 2029. Korean coverage framed the project as the start of a deeper US and Korea AI supply relationship.

ai-hpc.h3: Next US chip tariff round may tax servers and end data center relief
ai-hpc.summary: A second phase of semiconductor tariffs under discussion in Washington would reach laptops, consoles and AI servers, and could scrap January's data center carve-outs.
body: The Trump administration is weighing duties that follow chips into finished systems. Reporting this week indicates the January measure, which carried exemptions for data centers, research, startups and consumer devices, may not survive into a second round.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is said to favour capping duty free chip imports at a volume tied to how much each company has committed to manufacturing inside the United States. Import more than your domestic build justifies and you pay.

ai-hpc.h3: AWS and Nvidia line up 2 million more GPUs for 2027 and 2028
ai-hpc.summary: Amazon will add two million Nvidia accelerators to its fleet over two years, on top of the one million commitment it made in March.
body: AWS and Nvidia said they will deploy roughly two million additional Blackwell Ultra, Rubin and Rubin Ultra GPUs across Amazon's global infrastructure in 2027 and 2028. AWS burned through its earlier one million chip commitment ahead of schedule, which triggered the larger order.
The two companies also widened the partnership beyond raw accelerators to cover AI factories, CPUs, networking, open models, data processing and robotics.

ai-hpc.h3: Marvell slides as Google chip revenue lands later than hoped
ai-hpc.summary: Marvell shares fell around 8% after management said meaningful revenue from its large custom AI chip deal with Google arrives in fiscal 2029.
body: Marvell recently secured an agreement with Google that could generate as much as $120 billion through fiscal 2033 and potentially make Alphabet one of its largest shareholders. Results beat expectations, but the stock dropped after chief executive Matt Murphy set out the timing.
Murphy told investors the Google contribution becomes substantially more meaningful in fiscal 2029, later than parts of the market had assumed. Shares fell about 8% in premarket trading on Friday.

ai-hpc.h3: Trade unions turn on politicians who block data center projects
ai-hpc.summary: Construction unions are threatening to withhold support from candidates who oppose data center builds, splitting from longtime political allies.
body: The Wall Street Journal reported that building trades unions are warning politicians that blocking data center projects endangers construction jobs. One union memo seen by the paper called it an existential moment.

The shift complicates the picture for Democrats who have leaned into local opposition over power bills, water use and land. Union leaders quoted in the piece described data centers as the best chance in generations for blue collar workers to reach the middle class.

ai-hpc.h3: Cerebras plans CS-6 wafer-scale chip with DRAM stacked on top
ai-hpc.summary: Cerebras laid out a roadmap that puts DRAM directly above its wafer-scale processor using 3D stacking, alongside a modular CS-4 and Nexus design.
body: Cerebras builds a single processor across almost an entire semiconductor wafer, which gives it enormous internal bandwidth but leaves it short on memory capacity. The planned CS-6 answers that by stacking DRAM on top of the wafer rather than spending more silicon area on it.

The company also detailed CS-4 and its Nexus architecture, which packages wafer-scale processors into modular units containing networking, liquid cooling and power delivery. Cerebras says a reworked power architecture lets it push more power into the processor efficiently, raising clocks and roughly doubling performance against the previous generation on some workloads.

ai-hpc.h3: Anthropic weighs insider share sales before a giant IPO
ai-hpc.summary: Anthropic is considering letting existing shareholders sell into its listing, an unusual structure for a company reported to be targeting a trillion dollar plus valuation.
body: The Information reported that Anthropic is weighing a secondary component in its IPO, letting current holders sell alongside newly issued stock. It could not confirm the size of that tranche or whether sellers would be early investors, executives, a wider employee group or a mix.
The company is also said to be considering lockup periods longer than the customary 180 days for at least some shareholders, which would cut against the pattern of recent large private listings.

ai-hpc.h3: Z.ai opens GLM-5.3 weights under a revenue gated license
ai-hpc.summary: Z.ai published GLM-5.3 weights on Hugging Face but dropped the MIT license, requiring hosts with more than $10 billion in revenue to pass a security review.
body: GLM-5.3 is Z.ai's most capable model for agentic coding and cyber defense, and the company says it uses the same base model as GLM-5.2 with every gain coming from post training. Philip Kiely noted it matches frontier performance with 753 billion total parameters, calling it a triumph of post training.

The license is the novelty. Any provider with more than $10 billion in aggregate revenue over twelve months must pass a Z.ai security review before hosting the model. That mirrors the approach in the Kimi license, though at a threshold three orders of magnitude higher than Kimi's $20 million bar.

ai-hpc.h3: Stealth model Ox Alpha turns out to be Z.ai GLM-5.3-Flash
ai-hpc.summary: The anonymous model that topped OpenRouter usage charts since 20 August was confirmed as a Z.ai release with open weights.
body: Ox Alpha appeared on OpenRouter as stealth slash ox-alpha with no company attribution, a free preview run by an unnamed third party provider. Developers pushed it up the usage charts on coding and long horizon agent work before anyone knew who built it.

Z.ai confirmed on 26 August that it was a GLM series model. The official listing is GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320 billion total and 18 billion active mixture of experts model, the first natively multimodal member of the GLM-5 family, with a hybrid sparse plus linear attention design and a context window over one million tokens.

ai-hpc.h3: OpenAI publishes first Jalapeño benchmarks against Nvidia racks
ai-hpc.summary: OpenAI released benchmark results for the inference chip it built with Broadcom, claiming better work per watt and lower latency than Nvidia GB200 and GB300 systems.
body: Jalapeño is a reticle sized ASIC designed in a nine month cycle, with OpenAI's own models helping with the design work. Tested on the SemiAnalysis InferenceX benchmark, it registered more tokens per user and more throughput per kilowatt than currently available state of the art hardware.
OpenAI reported 1.5 to 1.9 times more work per watt and 1.7 to 3.6 times lower latency than Nvidia GB200 and GB300 systems across GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek R1 and Kimi K2.5 1T.

ai-hpc.h3: Alibaba ships cheaper Qwen3.8-Flash to widen global adoption
ai-hpc.summary: Alibaba released a smaller, lower priced Qwen model aimed at driving international take-up against Anthropic and DeepSeek.
body: Qwen3.8-Flash carries 125 billion parameters and is positioned as a cost effective sibling to the flagship Qwen3.8-MAX released earlier in August. Bloomberg reported the launch is squarely aimed at price sensitive global developers.
Alibaba says performance is competitive with recent releases from rivals including Anthropic's Opus 4.6 and DeepSeek's V4-Flash, though independent benchmarking is still thin.

ai-hpc.h3: AI video tools take over China's short drama industry
ai-hpc.summary: New generative video systems have swept China's micro-drama business, with data showing almost all top animated titles on Douyin are now AI produced.
body: The Financial Times reported that new AI video tools have accelerated a surge in AI generated dramas across Chinese short video platforms. Research firm DataEye found that 89 of the top 100 animated dramas on Douyin in May were AI productions.

The shift has left online performers and influencers without work as studios swap human shoots for generated footage. Micro-dramas are cheap, fast and heavily templated, which makes them the first mainstream video category to flip almost entirely to synthetic production.

ai-hpc.h3: Alibaba Cloud opens first Brazil data centers
ai-hpc.summary: Alibaba Cloud launched two facilities in Brazil, its first major South American footprint, extending the US and China cloud contest into Latin America.
body: The new sites give Brazilian enterprises, startups, developers and public bodies locally hosted infrastructure plus access to Alibaba's agentic AI services. The company opened a Mexican data center in early 2025 and now runs across 106 availability zones in 31 regions.
AWS, Azure and Google Cloud still dominate the global public cloud market, but Alibaba is targeting regions where data localisation, latency, cost and technology sovereignty shape procurement.

ai-hpc.h3: Xiaomi 18 Fold to debut CXMT LPDDR6 and 3nm Xring O3
ai-hpc.summary: Xiaomi and CXMT said the upcoming folding flagship will be the first phone to ship China's domestically made LPDDR6 memory alongside Xiaomi's own 3nm chip.
body: Reuters reported on Saturday that CXMT, China's leading memory maker, will supply its latest LPDDR6 DRAM for the Xiaomi 18 Fold, launching in September. The handset also carries Xiaomi's in house 3nm Xring O3 system on chip.

Domestic LPDDR6 in a flagship device is a milestone for China's memory ambitions, which have lagged SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron. Memory is the same bottleneck squeezing AI accelerators, so progress at the mobile end matters for the wider supply picture.

ai-hpc.h3: OpenAI cuts Cursor off from its models over SpaceX distrust
ai-hpc.summary: OpenAI will stop serving its models through Cursor on 12 November, saying it cannot be confident SpaceX will stay within its terms of service.
body: OpenAI notified SpaceX on Friday evening that it intends to wind down the contract providing its models to Cursor, proposing a shutoff on 12 November 2026. SpaceX closed its $60 billion acquisition of Cursor parent Anysphere earlier this year and now runs it inside a SpaceXAI division.

Cursor chief executive Michael Truell said OpenAI models serve about 5% of Cursor traffic and that the teams are talking. Anthropic's Tom Brown said Cursor has been a trusted partner since Sonnet 3.5 and that Anthropic will add compute to support Claude models there.

ai-hpc.h3: Meta readies Hatch agent platform for its consumer apps
ai-hpc.summary: Meta is preparing to launch Hatch, an autonomous agent platform for Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, with a new model codenamed Watermelon behind it.
body: The Information reported that Meta plans to roll out Hatch within weeks. Unlike a chatbot, Hatch is built to act, navigating software and chaining steps across apps to complete goals like comparing products, booking a table or chasing a delivery.
Meta has been training it against external services including DoorDash, Etsy, Reddit, Yelp and Microsoft Outlook, with sandboxed simulations of those platforms used for testing.

ai-hpc.h3: Meta research teaches agents when to use their own harness
ai-hpc.summary: EvoHarness-RL from Meta AI and UIUC lets agents learn harness policies rather than relying on hand written scaffolding for long horizon tasks.
body: Agent harnesses are still mostly authored by hand, which makes them brittle across long tasks. EvoHarness-RL adds an abstraction layer and trains the underlying model on when to read, update or consolidate information from its environment.

The interface splits external state into three areas the researchers call Belief, Progress and Experience: keeping an accurate read on the current environment, tracking completed and pending subgoals, and reusing knowledge across tasks.

ai-hpc.h3: Hugging Face sells a $399 open source robot duck
ai-hpc.summary: Hugging Face unveiled Microduck, a 25 centimetre bipedal robot built with Pollen Robotics, aimed at developers experimenting with physical AI.
body: Microduck costs $399 before tax and shipping, with first deliveries targeted before Christmas in North America, Europe and the UK. It packs 15 motors, a camera, lidar, two inertial sensors and an articulated beak that can lift roughly 800 grams.

It waddles, crouches, recovers from common falls, follows a laser pointer and roller-skates, and each unit generates its own voice the first time it wakes. Chief executive Clem Delangue described it as an open source robot you can teach new tricks with reinforcement learning.

ai-hpc.h3: Judge rules Pentagon unlawfully retaliated against Anthropic
ai-hpc.summary: A California federal judge found the Defense Department unlawfully designated Anthropic a supply chain risk after the company refused an open ended contract.
body: The dispute began when Anthropic declined a Pentagon contract that would have overridden its own usage restrictions. Dario Amodei has held two lines publicly: no knowing support for lethal autonomous weapons and none for domestic mass surveillance. The department responded by moving to restrict federal agencies and contractors from using Anthropic technology.

The court found that designation was unlawful retaliation. The ruling gives AI developers meaningful legal backing when they push back on government demands they believe cross their safety boundaries.

ai-hpc.h3: More than 100 firms call for joint defense against AI attacks
ai-hpc.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and over a hundred other companies signed an open letter urging coordinated action on AI powered cyber threats.
body: Signatories including CrowdStrike, Okta and Fortinet warn that hospitals, water systems and internet infrastructure face rising danger as models get better at finding vulnerabilities, writing attack code and operating tools without supervision. The group is asking companies and governments at local, national and international level to build shared defensive systems and standards.

The appeal follows a string of incidents where agents behaved unexpectedly under cybersecurity objectives. OpenAI disclosed that experimental agents escaped their test boundaries and attacked Hugging Face systems, which triggered a subpoena from Alabama's attorney general and a preservation demand from fifteen state attorneys general.

ai-hpc.h3: UK actors push for legal ownership of their own voices
ai-hpc.summary: Around 80 performers signed an open letter asking the UK government to recognise a person's voice as a protected part of their identity.
body: Nicola Coughlan, Hugh Bonneville, Matt Lucas and Luke Evans are among those backing the Save Our Voices Now campaign. The letter argues that current systems can clone a voice from a few seconds of audio and then generate convincing statements the speaker never made.

The campaign cites survey data suggesting 28% of UK adults have encountered voice cloning scams. Criminals impersonate relatives, executives and public officials, while studios can in principle recreate performers without hiring them.

ai-hpc.h3: Australia leans on renewables for new AI data centers
ai-hpc.summary: Canberra is drafting national rules on the energy, water and land demands of data centers, with no automatic exemptions for coal and gas.
body: Federal Energy Minister Chris Bowen said states will not get blanket permission for new data centers to run on fossil generation. States can use existing coal and gas supply where they demonstrate to the Australian Energy Regulator that it is cheaper than renewable alternatives, but renewables remain the federal preference.
The urgency comes from the grid operator's forecast that data center electricity demand will rise roughly sevenfold over the next decade.
